sources.title: End-to-End Object Detection with Transformers / DETR (Carion et al.)
sources.role: Discovery-bounded source used for factual verification

claims.text: Detection as direct set prediction: pair-wise matching cost (class-probability cost + L1 box cost + scale-invariant GIoU box cost) minimized by optimal bipartite Hungarian assignment; matched-pair Hungarian training loss (class NLL + L1 + GIoU box loss) plus Transformer encoder-decoder with learned object queries and parallel decoding; no anchors, no NMS, no specialized libraries.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 1/3.1/3.2 including loss equations and FFN/auxiliary-loss design.

claims.text: Results: COCO-val parity with heavily-tuned Faster R-CNN at equal parameters (42 AP R50, 44.9 DC5-R101); large-object dominance APL +7.8 attributed to global self-attention; small-object deficit APS -5.5; panoptic extension competitive (46 PQ test) especially on stuff classes.
claims.context: Full-paper sections 4.1/4.4 Tables 1/5; strengths and deficits both paper-stated.

claims.text: Costs stated by the paper: 300-500-epoch AdamW schedules (3 days on 16 V100), auxiliary decoding losses as standard training recipe after each intermediate decoder layer (shared FFNs; helpful, not architecturally mandatory), object-query slot specialization. DETR is designed to omit NMS in the final set-prediction pipeline; layer-wise ablation shows that NMS can improve the first decoder layer, but its benefit decreases with depth and becomes harmful at the final output; the paper interprets this as duplicate suppression emerging through decoder interactions/self-attention.
claims.context: Sections 4.1/4.2 ablations (encoder layers, decoder layers, FFN, positional encodings, NMS study) + conclusion challenges paragraph.

limitations.text: Small-object deficit and training cost are paper-stated open challenges; FPN-style successors address them outside this source.
limitations.context: Evidence boundary retained for downstream editorial use.

targets.finding: Full body consumed: loss formulation, architecture, COCO tables, ablations, panoptic extension, and stated challenges verified.

targets.finding: Bound primary paper re-verified read-only (already-bound locator; no new source). Removed overstrong necessity wording from claim-3; NMS study recorded as empirical ablation (helps layer 1, decreasing benefit, harmful at final; duplicate suppression via decoder interactions/self-attention). No necessity-proof language. Design contract (set prediction, Hungarian, cost-vs-loss, queries, NMS-free final pipeline, aux losses as recipe) preserved.
